title: How to Prepare for an SEO Audit Before Hiring
h1: How to prepare for an SEO audit before hiring
description: Prepare for an SEO audit: goals, target pages, access, search data, competitors, what an audit covers, how to prioritize fixes and what to ask a specialist.
intro: An SEO audit reviews your website to find what holds back its visibility in search results: technical problems, weak content, missing pages and poor links. A good audit gives you a short, prioritized list of changes. A weak one is a long automated report with little explanation. Preparation makes the difference. This article explains what to decide, what to gather and what to ask before you hire an SEO specialist.

faq.q: What does an SEO audit cover?
faq.a: Usually technical health, page speed, mobile use, content quality, keywords, internal links, and links from other sites.

faq.q: Will an audit improve my rankings by itself?
faq.a: No. An audit is a plan. Rankings change only when the recommended work is carried out and given time.

faq.q: How long before I see results?
faq.a: Search results often take weeks or months to change, depending on the site and competition.

faq.q: What access does the specialist need?
faq.a: Read access to your search and analytics tools is common, plus a way to view the site structure. Share access through each tool's user settings.

faq.q: Should the auditor also do the fixes?
faq.a: Decide this early. Some auditors only report, others offer implementation as a separate service.
